faq.lead: What dashAI is, what you need to run it, what happens to your data, and how far you can extend it. If your question isn't here, write to us: the answer ends up on this page.
faq.side.foot: Can't find your answer? Ask on Discord or open an issue.
faq.empty: No questions match your search. Try another term or write to us at contacto@dash-ai.com.
faq.general.p: The product in one line, what sets it apart, and who builds it.
faq.general.1.a:
An open-source, local-first desktop application for data analysis and Machine Learning model training without writing code. It covers the full cycle in a single interface: data import, exploration, training, evaluation, and explainability.

And it doesn't stop at predictive work: dashAI also covers generative AI. It includes language models, text-to-image generation, and RAG pipelines, with the same logic as always: everything runs on the user's own machine.

It runs on your own machine. There's no cloud, no account, and no external service behind it.
faq.general.2.a: Yes. The core is distributed under the MIT license: you can use it, modify it, and redistribute it, including in commercial contexts. There is no paid version, no reserved features, and no sign-up required to download it.
faq.general.3.a:
No, and the distinction matters. AutoML aims to automate modeling decisions. dashAI does something different: it is visual, interactive Machine Learning. It removes the code barrier, not your judgment.

You choose the model, define the data split, tune the hyperparameters, and read the metrics. The tool makes every step visible instead of solving it for you.
faq.general.4.q: Do I need to know how to code to use it?
faq.general.4.a:
Not for the main workflow. Loading a dataset, training a model, comparing it with another one, and reviewing its explainability is all done from the interface.

Python only comes into play if you want to extend dashAI: registering a new model, loader, metric, or explainer of your own.
faq.general.5.a:
It's a multi-year Chilean academic project, built by academics and students, backed by the Universidad de Chile (DCC and FCFM), the National Center for Artificial Intelligence (CENIA), and IMFD.

Development combines a stable engineering team with thesis students who contribute experimental features.
faq.install.p: Supported systems, ways to install, the security warning, and what hardware you need.
faq.install.1.q: Which operating systems does it work on?
faq.install.1.a:
Windows, macOS, and Linux, with one important caveat on macOS: it only works on Macs with an Apple Silicon chip, that is, the M series. Macs with an Intel processor are not supported.

On Windows and Linux there is no equivalent architecture restriction.
faq.install.2.a:
There are three paths, depending on how you work:

  • Desktop installer: the recommended route if you don't want to touch the terminal. Available on the download page.
  • PyPI: pip install dashai, on Python 3.11 or higher.
  • Docker: images for CPU and for CUDA, useful on servers and teaching labs.
faq.install.3.q: My system says the app is not safe or can't be verified. What do I do?
faq.install.3.a:
This is expected: the dashAI installers are not digitally signed yet. Signing requires a certificate purchased from Apple and Microsoft so their systems recognize the developer, and the project doesn't have one yet.

The warning doesn't mean there's anything wrong with the software: it's the default reaction of any system to an installer without a certificate. The code is public and auditable on GitHub, and you should always download from the official site or from the repository.
faq.install.3.mac.1: Drag dashAI to the Applications folder, like any other program.
faq.install.3.mac.2: The first time you open it, a warning will appear saying macOS could not verify the developer. Close that warning.
faq.install.3.mac.3: Open System Settings, go to Privacy & Security, and scroll down to the Security section.
faq.install.3.mac.4: There you'll see the message about dashAI with the Open Anyway button. Click it and confirm with your password or Touch ID.
faq.install.3.mac.5: The app opens and, from then on, launches directly without asking again.
faq.install.3.mac.tip: On older versions of macOS, the shortcut also works: right-click the app icon, choose Open, and confirm in the dialog.
faq.install.3.win.1: Run the installer. Microsoft Defender SmartScreen will show a blue screen titled Windows protected your PC.
faq.install.3.win.2: Click More info, the small link under the message.
faq.install.3.win.3: The Run anyway button will appear. Click it and continue with the normal installation.
faq.install.3.win.tip: If the downloaded file ends up blocked by the browser, right-click it, go to Properties, and check Unblock on the General tab before running it.
faq.install.3.note: Digital signing is on the project's to-do list. Once it's ready, these steps will no longer be necessary.
faq.install.4.q: What hardware requirements do I need?
faq.install.4.a: For work with tabular data and lightweight NLP, a standard desktop or laptop is enough. Generative models (LLMs and text-to-image) are the ones that push memory requirements up and, above all, benefit from a GPU.
faq.install.5.a:
It's not required. dashAI runs on CPU for the bulk of tabular data and text tasks.

If you have a GPU, the PyTorch backend takes advantage of it with CUDA (NVIDIA) or ROCm (AMD), which noticeably speeds up training and generative inference.
faq.install.6.q: My computer has a dedicated GPU and dashAI doesn't detect it. What should I do?
faq.install.6.a:
That's expected with the standard install: the desktop installers ship with CPU-only PyTorch, and pip install dashai installs the default PyTorch build, which is also CPU-only on Windows and macOS and never includes support for AMD GPUs on any system. dashAI still works, but all computation runs on the processor.

There are two ways to use your GPU:

  • PyPI with a GPU build of PyTorch: install dashAI with pip, then reinstall PyTorch from the index for your card: CUDA for NVIDIA or ROCm for AMD. If you plan to use language models (GGUF), also install llama-cpp-python with GPU acceleration. The exact commands are in the repository README.
  • Docker with CUDA: if your GPU is NVIDIA, the Dockerfile.cuda image already ships CUDA PyTorch and llama-cpp-python built with acceleration. Run it with docker run --gpus all; the step-by-step is in the Docker section of the README.

Either way, you need your card's drivers installed and, for Docker, the NVIDIA container runtime.
faq.install.7.q: How do I update to the latest version?
faq.install.7.a:
If you installed via PyPI: pip install --upgrade dashai. If you used the desktop installer, download the new version from the site.

Every release is documented in the repository's release notes.
faq.privacy.p: The most repeated question, and the reason behind the local-first design.
faq.privacy.1.q: Where does my data end up?
faq.privacy.1.a: On your machine. dashAI is a desktop application that reads and processes local files: it doesn't upload your datasets to any server, doesn't replicate them, and doesn't use them to train anything outside your computer.
faq.privacy.2.q: Do I need an internet connection?
faq.privacy.2.a:
Not for the core features: once installed, you can import data, train, and evaluate offline.

The connection is used at specific moments: installing the application, updating it, installing plugins from PyPI, and downloading pretrained model weights for the first time.
faq.privacy.3.q: Do I need API keys, an account, or a subscription?
faq.privacy.3.a:
No API is required. dashAI doesn't ask for an account, a subscription, or a model provider key to work: the models it includes are open-weight and run on your machine.

That said, the application does have a Credentials section, meant for cases where a particular component needs a credential: a gated model, or an external service you decide to connect. It's optional and the main workflow doesn't depend on it.
faq.privacy.4.q: Can I use it with sensitive or regulated data?
faq.privacy.4.a:
The architecture helps: since data never leaves your machine, a whole category of risk associated with uploading it to third-party services disappears. It's the reason the project presents itself as an alternative for working “without handing over data”.

Specific regulatory compliance, however, depends on the environment where you install the application and on your institution's policies.
faq.use.p: Product scope, model catalog, and supported data types.
faq.use.1.q: What can I do with dashAI?
faq.use.1.a: The complete pipeline, in a single interface: import a dataset, explore it, train predictive or generative models, evaluate them with metrics, and apply explainability techniques to the results.
faq.use.2.a:
Today there are 107 registered components, in two catalogs.

Machine Learning models: 75.

  • 15 classifiers for tabular data
  • 15 regression models
  • 15 text classification models
  • 10 machine translation models
  • 7 embedding generators
  • 6 image classifiers
  • 5 prompt templates for RAG
  • 2 vectorizers: TF-IDF and BM25

Generative models: 32.

  • 12 language models: Llama, Mistral, Mixtral, Qwen, Phi, and SmolLM2
  • 14 text-to-image: Stable Diffusion, SDXL, PixArt-Sigma, RealVisXL, and Tongyi Z-Image
  • 5 ControlNet pipelines for conditioned generation
  • 1 RAG pipeline

The catalog grows with every version, so the source of truth is the documentation: ML models and generative models.
faq.use.3.q: What types of data does it support?
faq.use.3.a:
Tabular data (classification and regression), text (classification, translation, and embeddings), and images, both for classifying them and for generating them from text.

The loaders are extensible, so the input format is not a fixed limit.
faq.use.4.q: Can I compare models and tune hyperparameters?
faq.use.4.a: Yes. Hyperparameter optimizers are one of the system's registrable components, just like models and metrics, and comparing experiments is part of the evaluation workflow.
faq.use.5.a: Yes. Explainers are one of the system's twelve base classes, which means explainability isn't an add-on: it's a first-class piece, extensible like any other.
faq.extend.p: How to add your own components and under what rules.
faq.extend.1.a: By inheriting from one of the system's twelve base classes: models, data loaders, metrics, optimizers, and explainers, among others. You register your component and dashAI treats it like any of the native ones.
faq.extend.2.q: Do I have to code the interface for my component?
faq.extend.2.a:
No, and this is the product's most distinctive architectural piece. The UI is generated from the Pydantic schema your component declares: the backend exposes the schema and the frontend renders the form without knowing it beforehand.

You define the parameters in Python and the interface appears on its own.
faq.extend.3.q: How do I distribute a plugin?
faq.extend.3.a:
As a PyPI package. Anyone who installs it will see it available inside dashAI with no extra steps.

The full procedure, including the structure the package must have and how to publish it, is documented in Plugin development / Upload.
faq.extend.4.q: What license does the project have?
faq.extend.4.a: MIT on the core: no copyleft clauses and no reserved proprietary components. The code is auditable, modifiable, and forkable.
faq.community.p: The project's active channels and how to contribute.
faq.community.1.q: How do I report a bug or suggest a feature?
faq.community.1.a: By opening an issue on GitHub. If it's a bug, it helps a lot to include your operating system, the dashAI version, and the steps to reproduce it.
faq.community.2.q: How do I contribute to the code?
faq.community.2.a:
The repository has two main branches: production, which is stable, and develop, where development happens. Clone develop to contribute.

The complete guide, with the kinds of contributions the project needs, is in the Contribute section.
faq.community.3.q: Where can I ask questions or follow the project?
faq.community.3.a: On the Discord server for conversation and peer support, and on the mailing list for release announcements. For everything else: contacto@dash-ai.com.

faq.cta.p: This FAQ is written from what the community asks. If something was missing, tell us: it gets added.
